summary: The note reviews a nationwide U.S. telecommunications outage on October 9, 2023 that lasted nearly 16 hours and affected providers such as GlobalNet and CommuniCorp. It describes economic and social effects on finance, small business, logistics, healthcare, education and international trade, with quotes from affected people and experts. It also covers the government response, proposed legislation and CommuniCorp's $2 billion resilience investment.
one_line: Report on the 16-hour nationwide U.S. telecom outage of October 9, 2023, its economic effects across sectors, and the policy and industry responses.
key_facts: The nationwide U.S. telecommunications outage occurred on October 9, 2023, beginning at approximately 9:15 AM Eastern Time and lasting nearly 16 hours.
Major service providers including GlobalNet and CommuniCorp were affected, leaving millions without internet, mobile networks or landlines.
The NYSE and NASDAQ reported significant trading anomalies tied to communication lags during the outage.
Joe Madison, a trader at Stratton Oakmont, said orders weren't going through and there was panic about positions that couldn't be monitored.
Emily Nguyen, owner of the craft store 'Homemade Heaven', reported zero online sales for the day of the outage.
Truck driver Michael Davidson lost GPS and communication systems and had to rely on road signs and guesswork to meet delivery deadlines.
Cardiologist Dr. Leo Richardson said his hospital reverted to paper records and delayed several non-critical procedures.
Senator Elizabeth Harmon pushed the proposed 'Telecom Stability and Security Act' to impose stricter regulations on providers.
Government task forces were initiated to address weak links in telecommunication infrastructure, with advisor Richard Kim urging significant investment in resilience and security.
Marcus Young of Digital Frontier warned the outage may have lasting impacts on investor confidence in tech firms and stressed redundant systems and back-up protocols.
Global supply chains faced coordination delays, and multinationals reliant on real-time data saw a temporary drop in stock prices.
On November 1, 2023, CommuniCorp CEO Samantha Wells announced an additional $2 billion investment in redundant pathways and emergency response systems.
Dr. Jennifer Park called the outage a 'wake-up call for bolstering our telecom infrastructures.'
During the outage people turned to radios, print newspapers and face-to-face conversations for updates.
